implementation_notes: This is the pattern's home platform: System.Data.DataTable is the in-memory record set and the typed DataSet designer generates strongly typed DataTable/DataRow subclasses plus TableAdapter classes that already act as the per-table gateway, so the Table Module is the partial class in which you add the rules. A typed DataTable implements IEnumerable<TypedRow>, so a rule over the whole set is a LINQ aggregation (orders.Sum(row => row.Total)) or a bulk DataAdapter update. The typed DataSet stack is legacy in modern .NET and EF Core is the recommended mapping for new code, so use this shape where the pipeline really is table-shaped - imports, grids, reports, batch recalculation - and keep the module free of entity objects.
pitfalls: A DataRow has no parameterless constructor and generated typed rows do not use nullable types: rows must be created through the table's NewXRow() factory and NULL is set with SetXNull(), so code that news up a row silently fails or writes the wrong null representation.
DataTable is not thread-safe: a module that caches or shares one DataTable across requests races on rows - create one table per request, even though the module itself is stateless.
